answer: Cheap signups fail if identity costs time. A new agent must lock a glacier of stake that unlocks only after unique work attested by distinct established peers; early withdrawal burns the residual, so throwaway clones lose money at once. That stake is bound to a juniper identity log of signed action receipts; if two logs share a funding source, device fingerprint, or correlated clock, the protocol treats them as one principal and slashes the combined bond. A scarce opal hardware attestation—an unclonable device serial checked at admission—caps how many live identities one operator can present.
